claims.text: TC4 is a Ti6Al4V alloy with an alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure.
TC4 has low hardness and poor friction and wear performance under extreme-stress conditions.
The proposed intervention deposits an Inconel 718 transition layer on TC4 and then a refractory HEA top coat by laser cladding.
Inconel 718 can serve as a thermally compatible transition layer between TC4 and a refractory HEA.
An inert atmosphere, optimized laser power and scanning speed, and preheating will produce controlled interdiffusion and minimal residual stress.
The Inconel 718 layer will create a functionally graded interface that bridges the coating and TC4 in composition and thermal expansion.
The graded interface will reduce abrupt intermetallic formation and thermal-expansion mismatch.
An Inconel 718 transition layer enhances metallurgical or interfacial bonding.
An Inconel 718 transition layer mitigates cladding stresses and reduces interfacial crack formation.
The refractory HEA top layer supplies high hardness and improved wear resistance.
The dual-layer coating will preserve the intrinsic mechanical properties and stability of the TC4 substrate.
The dual-layer system may approximately double surface hardness relative to untreated TC4.
The dual-layer system will reduce coefficient of friction and wear rate under high-contact-stress conditions relative to untreated TC4 and direct HEA cladding.
The dual-layer system will have fewer interfacial defects than direct HEA cladding.
Direct refractory-HEA deposition on TC4 has demonstrated poor bonding, cracking, and uneven coating properties.
The predicted improvements require precise control of laser power, scanning speed, preheating, and inert-atmosphere conditions.
Departures from the specified processing conditions may cause adverse phase formation and degraded interfacial bonding.
The magnitude of hardness and wear improvement depends on process-parameter tuning and possible unexpected phase formation.
The experiment compares untreated TC4, directly HEA-clad TC4, and dual-layer-coated TC4 using hardness, tribology, bending, SEM, and EDS measurements.
The hypothesis is falsified if the dual-layer specimens fail to improve hardness and tribological performance or have comparable or greater interfacial defects than both controls.
